passages.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
passages.sermon: The Word existed in the beginning.\r\nThe Word was with God.\r\nThe Word was God.
passages.original: Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἦν ὁ Λόγος καὶ ὁ Λόγος ἦν πρὸς τὸν Θεόν καὶ Θεὸς ἦν ὁ Λόγος

passages.text: He was with God in the beginning.
passages.sermon:
The Word was with God in the beginning.
The Word existed at the start.
God was present with the Word.
The Word and God were together from the beginning.
passages.original: Οὗτος ἦν ἐν ἀρχῇ πρὸς τὸν Θεόν

passages.text: Through Him all things were made, and without Him nothing was made that has been made.
passages.sermon:
The Word was with God in the beginning.
The Word was God.
God made all things through the Word.
Nothing was made without the Word.
Everything that exists came into being through Him.
passages.original: πάντα δι’ αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο καὶ χωρὶς αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο οὐδὲ ἕν ὃ γέγονεν

passages.text: In Him was life, and that life was the light of men.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was with God in the beginning.
Jesus had life in Himself.
This life came from Jesus.
This life was the light for all people.
passages.original: ἐν αὐτῷ ζωὴ ἦν καὶ ἡ ζωὴ ἦν τὸ φῶς τῶν ἀνθρώπων

passages.text: The Light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.
passages.sermon: The Light shines in the darkness.\r\nThe darkness has not overcome the Light.
passages.original: καὶ τὸ φῶς ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ φαίνει καὶ ἡ σκοτία αὐτὸ οὐ κατέλαβεν

passages.text: There came a man who was sent from God. His name was John.
passages.sermon: God sent a man.\r\nThis man’s name was John.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο ἄνθρωπος ἀπεσταλμένος παρὰ Θεοῦ ὄνομα αὐτῷ Ἰωάννης

passages.text: He came as a witness to testify about the Light, so that through him everyone might believe.
passages.sermon:
John was a man sent from God.
John came as a witness.
John came to testify about the Light.
God sent John so that everyone might believe through him.
passages.original: οὗτος ἦλθεν εἰς μαρτυρίαν ἵνα μαρτυρήσῃ περὶ τοῦ φωτός ἵνα πάντες πιστεύσωσιν δι’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: He himself was not the Light, but he came to testify about the Light.
passages.sermon: John was not the Light.\r\nGod sent John.\r\nJohn came to testify about the Light.
passages.original: οὐκ ἦν ἐκεῖνος τὸ φῶς ἀλλ’ ἵνα μαρτυρήσῃ περὶ τοῦ φωτός

passages.text: The true Light who gives light to every man was coming into the world.
passages.sermon: The true Light was coming into the world.\r\nThis Light gives light to every person.
passages.original: Ἦν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινὸν ὃ φωτίζει πάντα ἄνθρωπον ἐρχόμενον εἰς τὸν κόσμον

passages.text: He was in the world, and though the world was made through Him, the world did not recognize Him.
passages.sermon: Jesus was in the world.\r\nGod made the world through Jesus.\r\nThe world did not recognize Jesus.
passages.original: ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ἦν καὶ ὁ κόσμος δι’ αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο καὶ ὁ κόσμος αὐτὸν οὐκ ἔγνω

passages.text: He came to His own, and His own did not receive Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the true Light.
Jesus gives light to every person.
Jesus came into the world.
God made the world through Jesus.
Jesus came to His own people.
His own people did not receive Him.
passages.original: εἰς τὰ ἴδια ἦλθεν καὶ οἱ ἴδιοι αὐτὸν οὐ παρέλαβον

passages.text: But to all who did receive Him, to those who believed in His name, He gave the right to become children of God— children born not of blood, nor of the desire or will of man, but born of God.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Word.
Jesus came into the world.
Some people received Jesus.
Some people believed in Jesus’ name.
Jesus gave these people the right to become children of God.
These children of God were not born from human blood.
They were not born from the desire of the flesh.
They were not born from the will of a man.
God gave them new birth.
God made them His children.
passages.original: ὅσοι δὲ ἔλαβον αὐτόν ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν τέκνα Θεοῦ γενέσθαι τοῖς πιστεύουσιν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ οἳ οὐκ ἐξ αἱμάτων οὐδὲ ἐκ θελήματος σαρκὸς οὐδὲ ἐκ θελήματος ἀνδρὸς ἀλλ’ ἐκ Θεοῦ ἐγεννήθησαν

passages.text: The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us. We have seen His glory, the glory of the one and only Son from the Father, full of grace and truth.
passages.sermon:
The Word is Jesus Christ.
Jesus Christ is the one and only Son from the Father.
Jesus Christ became flesh.
Jesus Christ lived among us.
We saw His glory.
His glory is the glory of the only Son from the Father.
Jesus Christ is full of grace.
Jesus Christ is full of truth.
passages.original: Καὶ ὁ Λόγος σὰρξ ἐγένετο καὶ ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν καὶ ἐθεασάμεθα τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ δόξαν ὡς μονογενοῦς παρὰ Πατρός πλήρης χάριτος καὶ ἀληθείας

passages.text: John testified concerning Him. He cried out, saying, “This is He of whom I said, ‘He who comes after me has surpassed me because He was before me.’ ”
passages.sermon:
John spoke about Jesus.
John gave testimony about Jesus.
John cried out in a loud voice.
John said, “This is the one I spoke about.”
John said, “He comes after me.”
John said, “He has become greater than I am.”
John said, “He was before me.”
passages.original: Ἰωάννης μαρτυρεῖ περὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ κέκραγεν λέγων Οὗτος ἦν ὃν εἶπον Ὁ ὀπίσω μου ἐρχόμενος ἔμπροσθέν μου γέγονεν ὅτι πρῶτός μου ἦν

passages.text: From His fullness we have all received grace upon grace.
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ is full of grace and truth.
He is the one and only Son from the Father.
We have all received from His fullness.
He gives us grace upon grace.
passages.original: Ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ πληρώματος αὐτοῦ ἡμεῖς πάντες ἐλάβομεν καὶ χάριν ἀντὶ χάριτος

passages.text: For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
Moses gave the law.
Jesus Christ brought grace.
Jesus Christ brought truth.
Grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
passages.original: ὅτι ὁ νόμος διὰ Μωϋσέως ἐδόθη ἡ χάρις καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐγένετο

passages.text: No one has ever seen God, but the one and only Son, who is Himself God and is at the Father’s side, has made Him known.
passages.sermon:
No one has ever seen God.
The one and only Son has made God known.
The Son is Himself God.
The Son is at the Father’s side.
passages.original: Θεὸν οὐδεὶς ἑώρακεν πώποτε μονογενὴς Θεὸς ὁ ὢν εἰς τὸν κόλπον τοῦ Πατρὸς ἐκεῖνος ἐξηγήσατο

passages.text: And this was John’s testimony when the Jews of Jerusalem sent priests and Levites to ask him, “Who are you?”
passages.sermon:
John was a man who gave testimony about Jesus.
The Jews lived in Jerusalem.
The Jews sent priests and Levites to John.
The priests and Levites came from Jerusalem.
They came to ask John a question.
They asked John, “Who are you?”
passages.original: Καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ μαρτυρία τοῦ Ἰωάννου ὅτε ἀπέστειλαν πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἐξ Ἱεροσολύμων ἱερεῖς καὶ Λευίτας ἵνα ἐρωτήσωσιν αὐτόν Σὺ τίς εἶ

passages.text: He did not refuse to confess, but openly declared, “I am not the Christ.”
passages.sermon:
John was a man sent by God.
John spoke honestly.
John did not hide the truth.
John clearly said, “I am not the Christ.”
passages.original: καὶ ὡμολόγησεν καὶ οὐκ ἠρνήσατο καὶ ὡμολόγησεν ὅτι Ἐγὼ οὐκ εἰμὶ ὁ Χριστός

passages.text: “Then who are you?” they inquired. “Are you Elijah?” He said, “I am not.” “Are you the Prophet?” He answered, “No.”
passages.sermon:
Jewish leaders sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to question John.
They asked John, “Are you Elijah?”
John said, “I am not.”
They asked John, “Are you the Prophet?”
John answered, “No.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτόν Τί οὖν σὺ Ἠλίας εἶ Καὶ λέγει Οὐκ εἰμί Ὁ προφήτης εἶ σύ Καὶ ἀπεκρίθη Οὔ

passages.text: So they said to him, “Who are you? We need an answer for those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?”
passages.sermon:
A group of people came to John.
They spoke to John.
They asked John a question.
They said, “Who are you?”
They said, “We need to give an answer to those who sent us.”
They said, “What do you say about yourself?”
passages.original: Εἶπαν οὖν αὐτῷ Τίς εἶ ἵνα ἀπόκρισιν δῶμεν τοῖς πέμψασιν ἡμᾶς τί λέγεις περὶ σεαυτοῦ

passages.text: John replied in the words of Isaiah the prophet: “I am a voice of one calling in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way for the Lord.’ ”
passages.sermon:
John spoke to the people who questioned him.
John used the words of Isaiah the prophet.
John said, “I am a voice calling in the wilderness.”
John said, “Make straight the way for the Lord.”
Isaiah the prophet first spoke these words.
passages.original: Ἔφη Ἐγὼ φωνὴ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ Εὐθύνατε τὴν ὁδὸν Κυρίου καθὼς εἶπεν Ἠσαΐας ὁ προφήτης

passages.text: Then the Pharisees who had been sent asked him, “Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?”
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees sent men to John.
These men asked John a question.
They said to John, “Why do you baptize people?”
They said, “You are not the Christ.”
They said, “You are not Elijah.”
They said, “You are not the Prophet.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀπεσταλμένοι ἦσαν ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτὸν καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Τί οὖν βαπτίζεις εἰ σὺ οὐκ εἶ ὁ Χριστὸς οὐδὲ Ἠλίας οὐδὲ ὁ προφήτης

passages.text: “I baptize with water,” John replied, “but among you stands One you do not know.
passages.sermon:
John spoke to the Pharisees who questioned him.
John was a prophet who baptized people.
John said, “I baptize with water.”
There is a person standing among you.
You do not know this person.
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰωάννης λέγων Ἐγὼ βαπτίζω ἐν ὕδατι μέσος ὑμῶν ἕστηκεν ὃν ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε

passages.text: He is the One who comes after me, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie.”
passages.sermon:
John the Baptist spoke to the Pharisees.
John said, “Someone is coming after me.
This person stands among you now.
You do not know Him.
He is greater than I am.
I am not worthy to untie the straps of His sandals.”
passages.original: ὁ ὀπίσω μου ἐρχόμενος οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐγὼ ἄξιος ἵνα λύσω αὐτοῦ τὸν ἱμάντα τοῦ ὑποδήματος

passages.text: All this happened at Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
passages.sermon:
John was baptizing people.
He was at Bethany.
Bethany was beyond the Jordan River.
All these things happened there.
passages.original: Ταῦτα ἐν Βηθανίᾳ ἐγένετο πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου ὅπου ἦν ὁ Ἰωάννης βαπτίζων

passages.text: The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, “Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!
passages.sermon:
John was a prophet.
John baptized people at Bethany, beyond the Jordan.
The next day, John saw Jesus.
Jesus was coming toward John.
John spoke to the people.
John said, “Look, the Lamb of God.
He takes away the sin of the world.”
passages.original: Τῇ ἐπαύριον βλέπει τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐρχόμενον πρὸς αὐτόν καὶ λέγει Ἴδε ὁ Ἀμνὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ὁ αἴρων τὴν ἁμαρτίαν τοῦ κόσμου

passages.text: This is He of whom I said, ‘A man who comes after me has surpassed me because He was before me.’
passages.sermon:
John was a prophet.
John baptized people at Bethany beyond the Jordan.
John saw Jesus coming toward him.
John spoke about Jesus.
John said, “This is the man I spoke about.”
John said, “He comes after me.”
John said, “He has surpassed me.”
John said, “He was before me.”
passages.original: οὗτός ἐστιν ὑπὲρ οὗ ἐγὼ εἶπον Ὀπίσω μου ἔρχεται ἀνὴρ ὃς ἔμπροσθέν μου γέγονεν ὅτι πρῶτός μου ἦν

passages.text: I myself did not know Him, but the reason I came baptizing with water was that He might be revealed to Israel.”
passages.sermon:
John was a prophet.
John spoke about Jesus.
John said, “I did not know Jesus.”
God sent John to baptize people with water.
John baptized with water for a reason.
John baptized so that Jesus would be revealed to Israel.
passages.original: κἀγὼ οὐκ ᾔδειν αὐτόν ἀλλ’ ἵνα φανερωθῇ τῷ Ἰσραὴλ διὰ τοῦτο ἦλθον ἐγὼ ἐν ὕδατι βαπτίζων

passages.text: Then John testified, “I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove and resting on Him.
passages.sermon:
John was a prophet.
John spoke to the people.
John gave his testimony.
John said, “I saw the Spirit.
The Spirit came down from heaven.
The Spirit came down like a dove.
The Spirit rested on Him.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐμαρτύρησεν Ἰωάννης λέγων ὅτι Τεθέαμαι τὸ Πνεῦμα καταβαῖνον ὡς περιστερὰν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἔμεινεν ἐπ’ αὐτόν

passages.text: I myself did not know Him, but the One who sent me to baptize with water told me, ‘The man on whom you see the Spirit descend and rest is He who will baptize with the Holy Spirit.’
passages.sermon:
John was a prophet.
God sent John to baptize people with water.
John did not know Jesus at first.
God spoke to John.
God gave John a sign.
God said, “You will see the Spirit come down and stay on a man.”
God said, “This man will baptize with the Holy Spirit.”
The man who receives the Spirit is the one God chose.
This man is Jesus.
passages.original: κἀγὼ οὐκ ᾔδειν αὐτόν ἀλλ’ ὁ πέμψας με βαπτίζειν ἐν ὕδατι ἐκεῖνός μοι εἶπεν Ἐφ’ ὃν ἂν ἴδῃς τὸ Πνεῦμα καταβαῖνον καὶ μένον ἐπ’ αὐτόν οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ βαπτίζων ἐν Πνεύματι Ἁγίῳ

passages.text: I have seen and testified that this is the Son of God.”
passages.sermon:
John is speaking.
\r\nJohn saw Jesus.
\r\nJohn gave testimony about Jesus.
\r\nJohn said, "This is the Son of God."
passages.original: κἀγὼ ἑώρακα καὶ μεμαρτύρηκα ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: The next day John was there again with two of his disciples.
passages.sermon:
John was a prophet.
He baptized people in water.
God sent John to baptize.
The next day, John stood in the same place.
Two of John’s disciples were with him.
passages.original: Τῇ ἐπαύριον πάλιν εἱστήκει ὁ Ἰωάννης καὶ ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ δύο

passages.text: When he saw Jesus walking by, he said, “Look, the Lamb of God!”
passages.sermon:
John was a prophet.
\r\nJohn had disciples.
\r\nJohn saw Jesus walking.
\r\nJohn spoke.
\r\nJohn said, “Look.”
\r\nJohn said, “This is the Lamb of God.”
passages.original: καὶ ἐμβλέψας τῷ Ἰησοῦ περιπατοῦντι λέγει Ἴδε ὁ Ἀμνὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: And when the two disciples heard him say this, they followed Jesus.
passages.sermon:
John was a prophet.
John had two disciples with him.
John spoke about Jesus.
The two disciples heard John speak.
The two disciples listened to John’s words.
The two disciples followed Jesus.
passages.original: καὶ ἤκουσαν οἱ δύο μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος καὶ ἠκολούθησαν τῷ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: Jesus turned and saw them following. “What do you want?” He asked. They said to Him, “Rabbi” (which means Teacher), “where are You staying?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw two men following Him.
Jesus turned to them.
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus asked, “What do you want?”
The two men answered Him.
They called Him “Rabbi.”
“Rabbi” means “Teacher.”
They asked Jesus, “Where are you staying?”
passages.original: Στραφεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ θεασάμενος αὐτοὺς ἀκολουθοῦντας λέγει αὐτοῖς Τί ζητεῖτε Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Ῥαββί ὃ λέγεται μεθερμηνευόμενον Διδάσκαλε Ποῦ μένεις

passages.text: “Come and see,” He replied. So they went and saw where He was staying, and spent that day with Him. It was about the tenth hour.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the two disciples.
He said, “Come and see.”
The two disciples went with Jesus.
They saw where Jesus was staying.
They stayed with Jesus that day.
It was about the tenth hour.
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτοῖς Ἔρχεσθε καὶ ὄψεσθε ἦλθαν οὖν καὶ εἶδαν ποῦ μένει καὶ παρ’ αὐτῷ ἔμειναν τὴν ἡμέραν ἐκείνην ὥρα ἦν ὡς δεκάτη

passages.text: Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, was one of the two who heard John’s testimony and followed Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Andrew was Simon Peter’s brother.
Andrew heard John’s testimony.
Andrew was one of two men who heard John.
Andrew followed Jesus.
passages.original: Ἦν Ἀνδρέας ὁ ἀδελφὸς Σίμωνος Πέτρου εἷς ἐκ τῶν δύο τῶν ἀκουσάντων παρὰ Ἰωάννου καὶ ἀκολουθησάντων αὐτῷ

passages.text: He first found his brother Simon and told him, “We have found the Messiah” (which is translated as Christ).
passages.sermon:
Andrew was Simon Peter’s brother.
Andrew was one of the two who heard John’s testimony and followed Jesus.
Andrew first found his own brother Simon.
Andrew spoke to Simon.
Andrew said, “We have found the Messiah.”
Messiah means Christ.
passages.original: εὑρίσκει οὗτος πρῶτον τὸν ἀδελφὸν τὸν ἴδιον Σίμωνα καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Εὑρήκαμεν τὸν Μεσσίαν ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον Χριστός

passages.text: Andrew brought him to Jesus, who looked at him and said, “You are Simon son of John. You will be called Cephas” (which is translated as Peter).
passages.sermon:
Andrew was Simon Peter’s brother.
Andrew brought Simon to Jesus.
Jesus looked at Simon.
Jesus spoke to Simon.
Jesus said, “You are Simon, son of John.”
Jesus said, “You will be called Cephas.”
Cephas means Peter.
passages.original: ἤγαγεν αὐτὸν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐμβλέψας αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Σὺ εἶ Σίμων ὁ υἱὸς Ἰωάννου σὺ κληθήσῃ Κηφᾶς ὃ ἑρμηνεύεται Πέτρος

passages.text: The next day Jesus decided to set out for Galilee. Finding Philip, He told him, “Follow Me.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
The next day, Jesus wanted to go to Galilee.
Jesus found Philip.
Jesus said to Philip, "Follow Me."
passages.original: Τῇ ἐπαύριον ἠθέλησεν ἐξελθεῖν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν καὶ εὑρίσκει Φίλιππον καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἀκολούθει μοι

passages.text: Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the same town as Andrew and Peter.
passages.sermon:
Philip came from Bethsaida.
Bethsaida was a town.
Andrew and Peter also came from Bethsaida.
Philip, Andrew, and Peter were from the same town.
passages.original: ἦν δὲ ὁ Φίλιππος ἀπὸ Βηθσαϊδά ἐκ τῆς πόλεως Ἀνδρέου καὶ Πέτρου

passages.text: Philip found Nathanael and told him, “We have found the One Moses wrote about in the Law, the One the prophets foretold—Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.”
passages.sermon:
Philip was from Bethsaida.
Bethsaida was the town of Andrew and Peter.
Philip found Nathanael.
Philip spoke to Nathanael.
Philip said, “We have found Jesus.”
Jesus is the son of Joseph.
Jesus is from Nazareth.
Moses wrote about Jesus in the Law.
The prophets also wrote about Jesus.
Philip said, “We have found the One Moses and the prophets wrote about.”
This One is Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.
passages.original: Εὑρίσκει Φίλιππος τὸν Ναθαναὴλ καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Ὃν ἔγραψεν Μωϋσῆς ἐν τῷ νόμῳ καὶ οἱ προφῆται εὑρήκαμεν Ἰησοῦν υἱὸν τοῦ Ἰωσὴφ τὸν ἀπὸ Ναζαρέτ

passages.text: “Can anything good come from Nazareth?” Nathanael asked. “Come and see,” said Philip.
passages.sermon:
Nathanael spoke to Philip.
Nathanael asked a question.
Nathanael said, “Can anything good come from Nazareth?”
Philip answered Nathanael.
Philip said, “Come and see.”
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ναθαναήλ Ἐκ Ναζαρὲτ δύναταί τι ἀγαθὸν εἶναι Λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Φίλιππος Ἔρχου καὶ ἴδε

passages.text: When Jesus saw Nathanael approaching, He said of him, “Here is a true Israelite, in whom there is no deceit.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him.
Jesus spoke about Nathanael.
Jesus said, “Here is a true Israelite.”
Jesus said, “There is no deceit in him.”
passages.original: Εἶδεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὸν Ναθαναὴλ ἐρχόμενον πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ λέγει περὶ αὐτοῦ Ἴδε ἀληθῶς Ἰσραηλίτης ἐν ᾧ δόλος οὐκ ἔστιν

passages.text: “How do You know me?” Nathanael asked. Jesus replied, “Before Philip called you, I saw you under the fig tree.”
passages.sermon:
Nathanael spoke to Jesus.
Nathanael asked Jesus a question.
Nathanael said, “How do you know me?”
Jesus answered Nathanael.
Jesus said, “Before Philip called you, I saw you.”
Jesus said, “I saw you when you were under the fig tree.”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ Ναθαναήλ Πόθεν με γινώσκεις Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Πρὸ τοῦ σε Φίλιππον φωνῆσαι ὄντα ὑπὸ τὴν συκῆν εἶδόν σε

passages.text: “Rabbi,” Nathanael answered, “You are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!”
passages.sermon:
Nathanael spoke to Jesus.
Nathanael called Jesus “Rabbi.”
Nathanael said, “You are the Son of God.”
Nathanael said, “You are the King of Israel.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ Ναθαναήλ Ῥαββί σὺ εἶ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ σὺ Βασιλεὺς εἶ τοῦ Ἰσραήλ

passages.text: Jesus said to him, “Do you believe just because I told you I saw you under the fig tree? You will see greater things than these.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Nathanael.
Jesus had just told Nathanael that He saw him under the fig tree before Philip called him.
Jesus asked Nathanael if he believed only because of this.
Jesus said Nathanael would see greater things than this.
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ὅτι εἶπόν σοι ὅτι εἶδόν σε ὑποκάτω τῆς συκῆς πιστεύεις μείζω τούτων ὄψῃ

passages.text: Then He declared, “Truly, truly, I tell you, you will all see heaven open and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Nathanael and the other disciples.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus is the King of Israel.
Jesus is also called the Son of Man.
Jesus said, “Truly, truly, I tell you this.”
“You will all see heaven open.”
“You will see the angels of God going up.”
“You will see the angels of God coming down.”
“The angels will go up and come down on the Son of Man.”
passages.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὄψεσθε τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀνεῳγότα καὶ τοὺς ἀγγέλους τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀναβαίνοντας καὶ καταβαίνοντας ἐπὶ τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου
